change_interpretations.engineering_summary: The transient pedal spike filter threshold was reduced from 10 ms to 5 ms, meaning only pedal spikes shorter than 5 ms will be ignored. Tests verifying spike rejection must be updated to use pulse durations under 5 ms.

assessments.reason: This test verifies torque response latency (94 ms measured vs 100 ms limit) following validated pedal input under unchanged VCU-DR-01. It does not test transient pedal spike filtering.
evidence: requirement_reference_raw: VCU-DR-01
procedure: Step validated accelerator demand to 75%; confirm requested positive torque no later than 100 ms after pedal validation.
assessments.recommended_action: Retain existing test procedure and baseline for VCU-DR-01 verification.

assessments.reason: The test assesses brake override priority over accelerator pedal demand under unchanged requirements VCU-DR-01 and VCU-BRK-03. It does not exercise transient pedal filtering.
evidence: requirement_reference_raw: VCU-DR-01; VCU-BRK-03
procedure: Apply 85% pedal with emergency-brake input; inspect torque and pressure command priorities.
assessments.recommended_action: No action required; proceed with standard regression testing.

assessments.reason: Although the requirement link is missing, the procedure explicitly tests torque transient response time under demand sweeps (recorded 92 ms). It does not test transient pedal spike filtering under VCU-DR-02.
evidence: procedure: Sweep demand 75–95% at nominal and high-load cases; recorded maximum 92 ms.
workshop_notes: High-load campaign did not keep all requirement hyperlinks after migration.
assessments.recommended_action: Restore the missing requirement link to VCU-DR-01 during next register reconciliation.

assessments.reason: This test evaluates emergency brake command latency under VCU-BRK-03 and uses a separate measurement clock from positive torque response as noted in workshop notes. It is unrelated to VCU-DR-02.
evidence: requirement_reference_raw: VCU-BRK-03
workshop_notes: Brake command latency and positive torque command latency are measured by different clocks.
assessments.recommended_action: Maintain existing test procedure for emergency brake latency.

assessments.reason: The test verifies controller degraded mode entry and fault logging upon wheel-speed sensor failure under VCU-DGN-04, which is unchanged.
evidence: requirement_reference_raw: VCU-DGN-04
procedure: Unplug simulated wheel-speed sensor and confirm degraded mode + fault log.

assessments.reason: This test verifies audit trail logging of drive mode changes under VCU-LOG-05, which is unaffected by pedal spike filter threshold updates.
evidence: requirement_reference_raw: VCU-LOG-05
procedure: Change Comfort to Sport; log timestamp and build identifier.

assessments.reason: Traceability is incomplete with a TBD requirement link and explicitly flagged unclear ownership, making its intended target requirement uncertain.
evidence: requirement_reference_raw: TBD
comment: Ownership and source link to be clarified
previous_result: NOT RUN
assessments.recommended_action: Assign an owner to clarify requirement mapping and verify if thermal response definitions reference pedal input filtering.

assessments.reason: The test references an unknown legacy requirement ID (VCU-OLD-88) from an outdated catalog, leaving requirement traceability broken.
evidence: requirement_reference_raw: VCU-OLD-88
parsed_links status: unknown_requirement
comment: Imported row; requirements catalog changed
assessments.recommended_action: Reconcile VCU-OLD-88 against current requirements catalog to establish valid traceability.

assessments.reason: The test evaluates qualitative torque ramp profile differences between Sport and Comfort modes under VCU-MOD-06, which remains unchanged.
evidence: requirement_reference_raw: VCU-MOD-06
procedure: Compare accelerator response under Sport vs Comfort during ramp and release.

assessments.reason: The test procedure injects a 7 ms false pedal pulse expecting it to be filtered. Under revised VCU-DR-02, only spikes shorter than 5 ms are ignored, rendering the 7 ms test pulse invalid for verifying spike suppression.
evidence: procedure: Inject 7 ms false pedal pulse and verify no propagated torque request.
VCU-DR-02 new_text: ...shall ignore transient spikes shorter than 5 milliseconds.
numeric_changes: 10 milliseconds to 5 milliseconds
assessments.recommended_action: Update the test procedure and script to inject a pulse shorter than 5 ms (e.g. 3-4 ms) to verify spike filtering, and add a test case for pulses > 5 ms.

assessments.reason: The test verifies positive torque cancellation during emergency braking under VCU-BRK-03, which is unaffected by VCU-DR-02.
evidence: requirement_reference_raw: VCU-BRK-03
procedure: While demand is high, request emergency braking and verify positive torque drops according to brake priority.

assessments.reason: The test checks platform ECU power-cycle startup readiness (433 ms vs 500 ms target), which is completely unrelated to driver pedal signal filtering.
evidence: procedure: Power cycle the ECU; verify readiness within 500 ms.
comment: Platform startup only
